extracted.intended_audience: psychologists, psychometricians, and researchers validating personality/humor inventories (especially STCI) in cross-cultural settings
extracted.subtask_description: Psychometric validation and standard-form development of the State‑Trait‑Cheerfulness‑Inventory (STCI) in a Mainland China undergraduate sample, including translation, item selection, factor analyses, reliability, and predictive validity with life satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑factor construct (cheerfulness, seriousness, bad mood) as states and traits
rubrics_metrics.description: The STCI incorporates cheerfulness (CH), seriousness (SE), and bad mood (BM) as both traits (STCI‑T) and states (STCI‑S), which form the affective and attitudinal basis of the sense of humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each trait/state has definitional facets (trait CH: CH1–CH5; trait SE: SE1–SE6; trait BM: BM1–BM5; state facets differ slightly). Validation should demonstrate these three factors both for trait and state forms (the paper reports three factors for both short forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation procedure (Brislin back‑translation method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chinese translation of STCI followed Brislin’s back‑translation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: two independent translators translate items into Chinese; Step 2: compare translations and produce a first Chinese item list; Step 3: back‑translate to English by other translators; original author reviews back‑translation; finalize translation after discussions and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item selection criteria for standard short forms (STCI‑T<60>, STCI‑S<30>)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of items for the short standard forms was based on multiple corrected item‑total correlation criteria and facet representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criteria (as in Ruch et al., 1996) used here: (a) corrected item‑total correlation (facet) ≥ 0.25; (b) corrected item‑total correlation (scale) ≥ 0.20; (c) corrected item‑total correlation (citc) with its own scale must exceed the ones of any other scale by at least 0.05; (d) all facets selected should be represented by an equal proportion of the long version (i.e., target numbers of items per construct in STCI‑T<60> after elimination: 21 CH, 21 SE, 18 BM). Items were eliminated iteratively if they didn’t meet these criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Scales and facets should show acceptable to high internal consistency as measured by Cronbach's alpha.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports Cronbach alphas for long and short forms (examples: STCI‑T<106> scales 0.86–0.96; STCI‑T<60> scales 0.84–0.94; STCI‑S<30> scales 0.67–0.94). Short‑form development aimed to maintain or improve alpha; increases in mean corrected item‑total correlations (citc) were used as evidence of preserved/improved quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retest reliability / temporal stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Retest reliability (test–retest) is expected to be acceptable for trait forms over short intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported retest reliabilities for STCI‑T forms in prior work: e.g., 0.77–0.86 for STCI‑T<106> (4‑week interval) and 0.73–0.86 for STCI‑T<60> (3‑week interval). Such values are used as benchmarks for temporal stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: EFA was used to examine facet clustering and to decide number of factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain factors with eigenvalues > 1 and use the scree test; inspect unrotated solution for cluster structure around centroids; apply oblique rotation when factors are not orthogonal. In this study EFA suggested three factors explaining the majority of variance (e.g., 67.5% for STCI‑T<60>, 55.8% for STCI‑S<30>).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) fit indices and cutoff guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple fit indices to judge model fit; particular benchmarks are given in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seven indices mentioned with cutoffs: (1) χ2/df where a value < 3 indicates acceptable fit; (2) RMSEA where ≤ 0.05 indicates good fit and values up to 0.08 indicate acceptable fit; (3) SRMR where ≤ 0.05 indicates good fit and up to 0.08 acceptable; (4) TLI and (5) CFI where values > 0.90 indicate acceptable fit. The STCI‑T<60> and STCI‑S<30> models achieved acceptable/good fit (example: χ2/df = 2.41; RMSEA = 0.07–0.08; SRMR = 0.05–0.08; TLI = 0.95–0.96; CFI = 0.96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Split‑sample validation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use separate subsamples for exploratory and confirmatory analyses to avoid capitalizing on chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this study the sample (N=476) was split into two groups (238 each) by odd/even record number; one group used for EFA and the other for CFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation targets for short forms (items per scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short standard forms should preserve representation across constructs/facets proportionally to the long form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STCI‑T<60> targeted 21 CH, 21 SE, 18 BM items (preserving facet proportions from STCI‑T<106>). STCI‑S<30> ended with CH=10, SE=8, BM=12 in the validated short form (see tables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercorrelation patterns expected among scales/facets
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected correlation pattern among cheerfulness, seriousness, and bad mood based on theory and prior findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cheerfulness should correlate negatively with bad mood (strong negative correlation) and negatively with state seriousness; seriousness should correlate positively with bad mood. Homologous state–trait correlations (e.g., state cheerfulness with trait cheerfulness) should be the highest among cross‑domain correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facet homogeneity / mean intercorrelation benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Facets within a construct should show substantial positive intercorrelations indicating homogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported average facet intercorrelations in this sample (examples): cheerfulness mean intercorrelation ≈ 0.63 (0.52–0.71), seriousness ≈ 0.40 (0.28–0.48), bad mood ≈ 0.70 (0.63–0.78). These can serve as empirical reference values for facet cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive validity criterion with life satisfaction (TSWLS)
rubrics_metrics.description: STCI scales should relate to life satisfaction in predicted directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect positive partial correlations between cheerfulness (trait and state) and Temporal Satisfaction With Life Scale scores, and negative correlations between bad mood and life satisfaction. In this study partial correlations (controlling for age and sex) showed significant relations (e.g., T‑CH total r ≈ 0.41; T‑BM total r ≈ –0.42). Additionally, STCI scales (as a group) accounted for ~22% of variance in life satisfaction in regression analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative item elimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Items failing to meet item selection/psychometric criteria should be iteratively removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the item selection rules repeatedly, monitoring effects on scale alphas, mean citc, and representation across facets until a satisfactory short form is obtained (the paper documents maintained or improved alphas and increased mean citc after elimination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model comparison and parsimony (test alternative factor models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate alternative factor structures (e.g., two‑factor, four‑factor) and show poorer fit if the hypothesized model is preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper tested two‑ and four‑factor solutions which had poor fit compared to the three‑factor model; this supports the three‑factor structure as preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for demographic covariates in correlational analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: When relating STCI scales to external criteria, control for age and sex where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial correlations controlling for age and sex were used to assess relationships with TSWLS; ANOVAs tested sex and age effects on STCI scales (the paper reports no sex or age effects in this young university sample).
